statement: Zhong et al. 2026 is a PRISMA review of 101 LLM-psychology papers in five domains (creativity, memory/metacognition, reasoning, problem-solving/executive control, ToM), formal search Apr 2025-Mar 2026, kappa 0.866 on 1,200 records
Zhong et al. treat JDM biases only as one of four problem-solving categories; no moral, psycholinguistic or learning family; no coding of robustness-reporting practices

Zhong et al. re-tested 14 studies (10 replication, 4 minor perturbation) on one model (ChatGPT-5.4, no thinking), no human between-site comparison, no Many Labs; appendix with per-study variants not in the PDF; translation has inconsistencies (template methods block, GPT-4 vs GPT-5.4)

Pagliaro 2026 is a primary experiment: 11 biases x 8 LLMs, K=3-5 non-crossed researcher-crafted prompt variants, N=100 per variant, T=0.7; sigma_sys = SD of Bias Strength Index across variants; 1/78 cells significant at variant level vs 27/43 in GLMM
Pagliaro compares with humans only qualitatively, no Many Labs data, option order not counterbalanced, single temperature; covers framing, anchoring, sunk cost (3 of our 4 effects)
Tang and Kejriwal 2024 is a narrative review (no PRISMA, no search dates, no study total) of decision-making biases, reasoning and creativity with human baselines; no robustness coding, no re-tests

GUIDE-LLM (Feuerriegel et al. 2026) is a 14-item Delphi-based reporting checklist (N=68 then 80; 29 candidate items); requires version/date, temperature/seed/runs, exact prompts, code; does not require perturbation, option-order, temperature variation, preregistration or tests; contamination only optional; no empirical audit

statement: Geva et al. 2025 SSRN 5498944: systematic selection of biases/experiments, meta-analysis and meta-regression (author post: 20 biases, 10 LLMs, preregistered); full text not read; prompt-variation design, human comparison and Many Labs use unknown
Contribution verdicts: C1 overlapping with Zhong (not scooped), C2 distinct, C3 distinct with partial concept overlap with Pagliaro (prompt-variant spread already estimated); Geva unread

The 2019 correction to Klein et al. (2014) (Social Psychology 50(3) 211-213, doi:10.1027/1864-9335/a000373) corrects allowed/forbidden (Rugg 1941), one anchoring df/N typo in Table 2 and the ICC paragraph; its corrected Table 2 still prints the retrospective gambler's fallacy as weighted d 0.61, 99% CI [0.54, 0.68], t = 24.01, df 5,940, N 5,942, and its corrected Table 3 still prints anchoring Q babies 59.71, Everest 152.34, Chicago 312.75, NYC 88.16. It therefore documents neither the gambler condition-coding error nor the anchoring row order found by the statistician (X0005-X0006). Its corrected Table 2 gives NYC N 5,372 (df 5,370), while the released data give 5,362 for that item (runs/ml1-verify/verify_ml1_part3.log): unresolved.
source: https://psycnet.apa.org/fulltext/2019-34530-002.html (Hogrefe OpenMind licence), read 2026-10-16 by CRP-S02 in the built-in browser

statement: Geva et al. 2025 (SSRN 5498944) is a preregistered primary study of 20 randomly drawn biases on 9-10 LLMs at two temperatures (0.7, 1.0) with one LLM-paraphrase repeat of the battery; it has no per-effect prompt-cell spread estimand, no variance decomposition, no option-order or response-format variation, no human between-site benchmark and no Many Labs; its meta-regression is on its own 360 experiments, not the literature. Verdicts: C1 distinct, C2 distinct, C3 distinct with partial design overlap (temperature, n>=50 per condition, zero-variance problem: SD zero in 36.1% of experiments).

Cui, Li and Zhou 2025 (Nature Computational Science 5(8):627-634, doi:10.1038/s43588-025-00840-7) replicated 156 scenario-based experiments from psychology and management with three LLMs (main-effect replication 73-81 percent).
